data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words 'Rishi' (seer or sage) and 'Vant' (seeker). The name Rishivant carries the meaning “Seeker of Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Rishivant usually hope their child will grow to embody seeker of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Rishivant belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Seeker of Knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rishivant total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Rishivant" evokes a sense of reverence for ancient Hindu sage-scholars, the Rishis, who were known for their profound wisdom and transcendental knowledge. This name serves as a reminder of the rich cultural heritage and deep spiritual philosophies embedded within the Hindu tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Rishivant" holds deep spiritual significance as it represents an individual who is on a quest for enlightenment, much like a Rishi, seeking wisdom and divine knowledge. It is a reminder of the inherent potential for spiritual growth and the importance of seeking inner wisdom and truth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rishivant: One who embodies wisdom (Rishi) and strength (Vant). On the spiritual path, he continually seeks knowledge and powers to serve and uplift others.

vedic_reference.note: Found in the Rigveda, symbolizing a person with the virtues of great sages and seers.

historical_references.reference: Rishyasringa, a sage mentioned in the Mahabharata, was the son of the sage Vibhishana and the vixen Twak. He was also known as Rishivant. Rishyasringa was an embodiment of the god Krishna and played an important role in the Mahabharata war.

Another reference to Rishivant can be found in the Puranas, where he is described as the son of the sage Agastya and the goddess Lopamudra. He was a great sage and is believed to have composed the Agastya Samhita, a text on Ayurveda.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Rishivant' has gained modern relevance across various platforms, reflecting its deep historical roots.
